# Potato late blight

## Summary for 2024

Late blight reached the potato rows on plot 14 before it reached the tunnel tomatoes, by almost two weeks. Hutton alert from BlightWatch for TQ13 came on 19 July, first lesions on the 'Charlotte' on 21 July, and I cut the haulms down on 23 July. The tomatoes went later, see [[Tomato blight]] for that sorry story.

## The rows

- 'Charlotte' (second early), 2 rows of 12, seed from Trago Mills, £4.99 per 2 kg net
- 'Sarpo Mira' (maincrop), 1 row of 10, from the allotment society shed order, ref WVA-SP-112
- 'Pink Fir Apple', 1 row of 8, saved seed from Colin Prowse

Planted 6 April 2024, earthed up twice, the second time on 18 May after the frost scare.

## How it showed

Dark, wet-edged blotches on the leaf tips first, with a pale fuzzy ring on the underside in the morning dew. Within two days the stems went black at the leaf joints. The 'Charlotte' collapsed fastest. 'Sarpo Mira' had two spots on one plant and nothing more all summer. 'Pink Fir Apple' went down by the 26th, which it always does, it is a lovely potato with no constitution.

## Cutting the haulms

### When and how

23 July, 6.30 in the morning before it got warm. Cut every stem of the 'Charlotte' and 'Pink Fir Apple' rows down to about 5 cm with the old shears, bagged the tops in builders' sacks and took them to the tip at Heathfield. Left 'Sarpo Mira' standing, picked off the two leaves by hand.

### Why not dig straight away

Derek Yeo's rule, which I've now written down so I stop asking him: leave the tubers in the ground for three weeks after cutting so the skins set and any spores on the soil surface die off before you lift. Lifting into wet blighted soil is how you get tuber infection in store.

## Lifting and yields

Lifted 12 and 13 August, dry days, about 19°C.

| Variety | Weight | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Charlotte | 18.5 kg | clean, small-ish |
| Sarpo Mira | 26 kg | huge, two over 600 g |
| Pink Fir Apple | 7 kg | 11 tubers with sunken rusty patches, binned |

Down on 2023 for the Charlotte (24 kg then) because they lost the last month of bulking.

## Storage

Dried on the shed floor for a day, then into hessian sacks in the garage. Garage thermometer says 6 to 8°C through the autumn. Checked the sacks every Sunday; found two soft ones in September, both Pink Fir. Colin's wife Brenda made an enormous [[Tortilla española]] with the last of the Charlotte in October and it was the best use they've ever been put to.

## Rotation and next year

Potatoes moved to bed 3 for 2025 as per the rotation in [[Gemüsebeet Fruchtfolge]]. No volunteers to be left in the old bed; I found 14 tiddlers from last year's crop when forking it over in March and pulled the lot, they carry it over. Growing only 'Sarpo Mira' and 'Charlotte' next year, and earlier: chitting from 1 February, planting by 30 March if the soil is above 7°C at 10 cm.

## Things I keep forgetting

- Sign up for BlightWatch again each spring, the registration lapses.
- Tomatoes and potatoes are the same disease, so don't put the tomatoes downwind.
- Wash the shears afterwards, and the boots.
